progress.text: A sheet keeps its own scroll position when sheets are inserted, deleted or moved before it: a new PivotTable or inserted sheet opens at the top instead of where its neighbour was scrolled; a closed window's positions are let go (#3485)

Form controls: Insert › Controls places buttons, sliders (scroll bars) and spin buttons on the sheet. A slider or spin button holds a whole number from 0 to 30000 in a linked cell (a drag or a held arrow is one undo step, and editing the cell moves the control); a button runs a macro or one command through the macro policy, asking first in a workbook opened from a file; Assign Action and Format Control edit them, and XLSX files read and write them (control properties, <controls> and VML), alongside the form controls GridCraft keeps unchanged

Dialogs take ranges by selection on the grid: reference boxes (RefEdit) with a collapse button that shrinks the dialog while the person selects, in Goal Seek, Solver (including the Model Range of Load/Save) and Data Analysis; while collapsed, the arrow keys move the selection and Shift+arrow extends it, and F4 cycles a reference's anchors

Python mode in the formula bar: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P, =PY then Tab, or editing a Python cell edits its code in the formula bar, with Enter for a new line, Tab to indent and Ctrl+Enter to commit through python.set. The code still doesn't run

Python cells as data: python.set stores code in a cell, Python cells copy, move, fill and undo like formulas, and .xlsx reads and writes Python cells as [MS-XLSX] specifies (xlfn.xlws.PY(index,0 or 1), the code in the workbook's Python part) with cached values and spills, so such workbooks open with their results; nothing runs Python (new code shows #BLOCKED!), and opening a file limits code size, result size and spill ranges

Equations: Insert › Equation (a split button with a gallery of examples) and an editor with quick-insert buttons, the error underlined at its position and a live preview; insert.equation and equation.edit; LaTeX laid out by RaTeX inside the new gridcraft-math crate, capped and panic-guarded, and cached on the shape so that painting never runs the layout engine; xlsx writes Office Math with a plain-text fallback and the source in descr, and reads Office Math back into LaTeX; PDF prints equations with the standard Symbol font and [?] for anything else

Solver writes a Sensitivity report: Simplex LP shadow prices, reduced costs and allowable ranges from the final tableau; GRG Nonlinear reduced gradients and Lagrange multipliers from difference gradients, at a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point only; Solver Results offers it where it applies (no score change)

Floating objects: charts, pictures, shapes and slicers share one selection with a frame of eight resize handles (each moves only its own edges, also on right-to-left sheets); Delete or Backspace deletes the selected object and Escape drops the selection; slicers follow row and column edits and sorts like the other objects; chart series follow cut-moves and sheet renames and deletes; a copied sheet gives its objects fresh ids; ui.inspect reports selectedObject and ui.object.select selects any object (#190, #213)

Chart data tables are available from Chart Design › Add Chart Element and Format Chart Area. Tables follow live source values and number formats, keep blank cells blank, offer legend keys and border settings, and survive XLSX save/reopen; the shared renderer includes them in print and PDF. Readiness estimates unchanged.

XLSX keeps the first visible workbook window's active sheet and display settings together, falling back to the first view when all are hidden. Tab ratios are normalized to 0–1000 on import and export; invalid numeric text uses 600. Synthetic round trips cover isolated attributes, missing views, and active tabs after sheet deletion/reordering; firstSheet remains separate #2264 work (#3057).
Esc in File › Info, Print or Options first leaves the text field; the next Esc returns to the sheet (#3035)

CSV and text open detects each column's date order: a value that reads only day first (31/05/2026) makes the column day first, a value that reads only month first (12/31/2026) makes it month first, an all-ambiguous column keeps month first with a warning, and a column with both kinds stays text with a warning (#2765)

Recently Used lists the functions most recently entered in a formula from any source (ribbon, control channel, MCP, scripts), kept with the preferences and returned by formulas.recentlyUsed; the Insert Function dialog takes Excel's title and a working category list (Most Recently Used, All, each category)

Formulas › Function Library as a big Insert Function button, the AutoSum split button and three columns of labelled small buttons, each category book in its own colour; category menus end with Insert Function… on that category; More Functions cascades into the remaining categories; Home › Editing shares the AutoSum menu; the MR key tip opens Recently Used
System and embedded CJK fallback text shares the Latin baseline in cells, editors and window titles (#1265, #2621). Symbol and emoji alignment, manual row heights and clipping are unchanged
Arabic bidi display/editing preserve logical source text; per-cell reading direction is editable and survives undo, XLSX and conditional-format priority
Arabic text shows in cells and the interface through a system, fontconfig or craft-fonts Arabic face; workbook fonts keep their script fallbacks

AutoSum over a selection does what Excel does: a selected row gets one total to its right (in its last cell if that is empty), not a one-cell total under each cell; a block whose last column is empty gets each row's total there, one whose last row is empty each column's, and with both the corner gets the total of the block; otherwise totals go under each column as before

Macro interface (macros.md): an Automate › Macros group (Record Macro, which turns into Stop Recording, Use Relative References, Run Macro with recent macros); "Recording · N steps" with Stop in the status bar; a Record Macro dialog (checked name, free Ctrl+Shift shortcut, description); the Macros dialog lists macros beside Automate scripts and a VBA project, with Run, Step Into, Edit, Create, Delete and Options; Ctrl+Shift+letter macro shortcuts; questions that offer Run, Overwrite, Shift Down or Shift Right; a step editor with a breakpoint gutter, drag to reorder, a command picker, reference boxes that switch between relative tokens and absolute references, Inputs and Output tabs, a debug bar (Check, Run, Step, Continue, Run to Here, Stop with keep or undo) and grid overlays for inputs, writes, conflicts and the current step

Go To lists the named ranges of every sheet (Sheet2!Name for a name scoped to another sheet; hidden names, constants and formulas left out) and the references entered before, a double-click goes to an entry, and the Reference box takes several names or references separated by commas (Price, Type, B14:C22,F19:G30)

Status bar: a right-click opens a menu that sets which selection statistics show (Average, Count and Sum by default; Numerical Count, Minimum and Maximum are new), kept with the preferences (view.statusBar)
Ctrl+Shift+U (Control+Shift+U on a Mac) expands and collapses the formula bar, on the grid and while editing (view.expandFormulaBar); on Windows and Linux it used to underline
Fill handle: from a date, the right-drag menu and the Auto Fill Options button offer Fill Days, Fill Weekdays (Saturday and Sunday skipped), Fill Months and Fill Years
PivotTables: Enable show details (pivot.options enableShowDetails); turned off, Show Details and double-clicking a value cell list no records, and XLSX files keep the setting (enableDrill)
PivotTables: right-clicking a value, subtotal or grand total cell offers Show Details in the cell menu, which lists the cell's source records on a new sheet as double-clicking does
Sheet tabs: dragging the handle between the tabs and the horizontal scrollbar gives the tabs more or less of the bar, as in Excel; each open workbook keeps its own share

Charts: 100% Stacked Area (insert.chart {type: "area", subtype: "stacked100"}), drawn as each value's share of its category's total; XLSX percentStacked area charts open as 100% stacked instead of stacked

Accounting negatives in text: $(1,234), $ (5) and (5)% read as negative numbers when typed, coerced by arithmetic or passed to VALUE, like Excel 365; (-5), ((5)), $5% and dates or times in parentheses stay text
Calc: INDEX(A1:C3,2) (one index on a reference of several rows and columns) is #REF! as in Excel, instead of the whole row; INDEX(A1:C3,2,) still gives the row

Formula hardening: digits too many for a finite number are text, so "1 <400 digits>/<400 digits>" no longer coerces to NaN; a NaN column index in VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP and the D-functions is #VALUE! instead of an index underflow; REGEXREPLACE stops building a result as soon as it can only be too long (a worst case went from 1 GB to 7 MB) (#2163, #2162)

View › New Window and Arrange All on the ribbon. Arrange All tiles, stacks side by side or top to bottom, or cascades the native windows over the main window's monitor, the active one first. Two windows on one workbook show different sheets without copying the workbook or marking it changed; Save records the sheet of the window used last. A dialog stays in the window it was opened in

On the desktop every workbook window is a native window of its own: New, Open and New Window open one, each keeps its own cell draft, dialog and ribbon, and the macOS menu bar acts on the window focused last. Closing one of several windows on a workbook doesn't ask; closing a workbook's last window, or quitting, asks about unsaved changes in that window. The last window closed quits on Windows and Linux; macOS keeps running with the menu bar. First craft-libs craft-window use (window list and viewport driver)

View › New Window opens a second window on the same workbook (it used to open a copy whose Save overwrote the original): each window has its own selection, active sheet and scroll, titles read "Book1:1" / "Book1:2", and Switch Windows, Hide, Unhide and Close act per window. The control channel, CLI send and MCP tools take an optional window or doc id and default to the active window; window.list (MCP listwindows) lists the windows

Typing in a cell and then choosing File › New no longer strands the first workbook: the entry is committed into its own workbook before any File or window command (a refused entry stays open and stops the command), View › Switch Windows and the macOS Window menu list the open workbooks with unsaved markers, view.switchWindows {doc} switches by a stable workbook id, and the macOS Quit item asks about unsaved workbooks

Page Setup paper sizes match Japanese Excel: B4/B5/B6 are the JIS sizes (ISO B4/B5/B6 stay reachable by name), so a Japanese B5 worksheet prints at 182×257 mm; Japanese Postcard (100×148 mm), Double Postcard (148×200 mm), Envelope #3/#4 (120×235/90×205 mm), Kaku #2/#3 (240×332/216×277 mm) and A6 are added, both sizes reach the PDF page (file.exportPdf/file.print MediaBox) and the size survives an XLSX round-trip; the Page Layout Size menu lists them. B4/B5 used to be the ISO sizes, which is changed here

Macro engine (macros.md): typed, declarative macros saved in the workbook (a JSON field; hidden names in xlsx); declared inputs checked with messages that name the cells; tokens (Input.col(2), Row, Output, Name:Total, {{…}} in formulas); one undo step with full rollback; a footprint dry run with ask, fail, overwrite, shift down or shift right; a policy that keeps macros away from files and the app, with approval for macros in opened files; Repeat, If and Stop steps; a debugger; a relative recorder; macro. commands beside the unchanged Automate scripts

Japanese interface catalog covers every key the Brazilian Portuguese catalog translates: the 398-label shared core plus 545 dialog, message, Backstage and menu strings (943 total, ~43% of ~2,200). A test parses pt.rs's source, so the two catalogs stay in step
Interface translated into Dutch (518 labels: ribbon, context menus, File view, dialog titles, Options); nl, nl-NL, nl-BE locale tags resolve to Dutch

Long flat operator chains (=A1+A2+…) up to Excel's 8,192-character limit (4,096 operands): entering, filling, inserting rows, undo, Evaluate Formula and XLSX save no longer overflow the stack; chains past 64 operands are saved as plain formulas, not dynamic arrays; Spanish formula entry accepts chains past 256 operands (#916)

Linux: "Use system setting" for the theme keeps following the desktop when the XDG Desktop Portal stops answering: each read gives up after 2 s and the next poll reconnects, where one unanswered call stalled the watcher for the rest of the session
